newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria says Forcados force majeure starts.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria says Forcados force majeure starts.

text.p: Royal Dutch Shell Group's Nigerian unit on Tuesday said force majeure affecting 80,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Forcados crude oil exports had come into effect and was expected to last between one and five days.

"Under the initial provision force majeure was expected to last until mid-May, but we expect that flow stations will soon be reopened and we will swiftly return to normal," a company spokesman told Reuters in Lagos.
He said no cargoes had been cancelled, only delayed.
Shell said agreement has been reached with local communities near the mid western oil-producing city of Warri for flow stations to be reopened after communal violence forced them to shut.
The spokesman said there was no indication that flow stations had yet been reopened but was hopeful that some would be reopened later on Tuesday.
Scores of lives have been lost in the past month during the conflict in Warri over the relocation of the local council headquarters from a Ijaw to an Itserkiri area.
Oil accounts for more than 90 percent of Nigeria's foreign exchange income and last week the army deployed troops into Warri in an effort to stop the fighting.
